findings.description: The `pup` skill table still says launches also hold when the plan's 5-hour window is at 85%. The PR removed that hold in code, in the conductor kickoff and in ADR 0156, but not here.
findings.body:
**Stale hold line in the `pup` skill**

The "Start a session for a task" row says `pup launch` and `pup new` "hold while a fresh usage reading (under 30 min) has the plan's 5-hour window at 85% or its 7-day at 90%". After this PR, `USAGE_WINDOWS` in `src/core/usage-limits.service.ts` holds only on `seven_day` at 90%, and a `five_hour` window is ignored.

The skill is the operator console's context (`README.md` links `skills/pup` into `~/.claude/skills/`; see ADR 0070). An agent or operator reading it would expect a hold at 85% of a 5-hour window that no longer exists, and could wait on it or misdiagnose a launch. It also contradicts the conductor kickoff this PR updated (`src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts:1389`).

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/20b1e1965bb3cf5330044c7796ed906ae0715934/skills/pup/SKILL.md#L38-L38
findings.suggestion: | Start a session for a task | `pup launch <task>`; `pup new "<goal>" --scope ...` plans and launches. Both refuse past the session cap (sessions awaiting review do not count) or under 1.5 GB of available memory; `--over-cap` (operator-only) lifts the cap, never the memory floor. Both also hold while a fresh usage reading (under 30 min) has the plan's 7-day window at 90%; `--over-limit` (operator-only) lifts that; `pup status` shows the reading |

findings.description: The USAGE_WINDOWS JSDoc's added "The plan has had no 5-hour window since 2026-11-09" is a dated changelog comment, which docs/conventions/general.md forbids ("No journal / changelog comments"). That history already lives in ADR 0156's amendment, so drop the sentence or shorten it to "a `five_hour` entry is ignored".
